name: Infosys
overview: Infosys is an Indian IT services and consulting company, founded in 1981 in Pune and headquartered in Bengaluru. It hires freshers mainly as Systems Engineers, with higher-paid Digital Specialist Engineer and Specialist Programmer roles for strong coders. Freshers train at the Infosys campus in Mysore.
variation_note: Systems Engineer and SP/DSE have different tests; sections, cutoffs and pay change by drive, college and year.

roles.title: Systems Engineer (SE)
roles.description: Main fresher role for application development, testing and support after training in Mysore.

eligibility.text: 60% (6 CGPA) in 10th and 12th, 65% (6.5 CGPA) in graduation
No backlogs at the time of the selection process; education gap of at most 2 years
Not eligible if you attended an Infosys interview in the last 9 months
For on-campus drives the criteria depend on the college

roles.title: Digital Specialist Engineer (DSE)
roles.description: Digital and full-stack role. Selected through the same coding test as SP, with a lower score threshold.

eligibility.text: 60% in 10th and 12th, 65% in graduation, no active backlog

compensation.text: 6.25 LPA plus a 75,000 joining bonus (as reported, 2026)

roles.title: Specialist Programmer (SP)
roles.description: High-level coding role for strong DSA and algorithm skills. Also offered through HackWithInfy pre-placement interviews.

eligibility.text: 60% in 10th and 12th, 65% in graduation, no active backlog

stages.name: Online test for Systems Engineer
stages.what: Computer-based test with several sections, each with its own cutoff. Covers maths, reasoning, English, pseudocode and puzzles.

format.text: 7 sections: Mathematical Ability, Logical Reasoning, Verbal, Pseudocode, Puzzle, English Grammar, English Writing
Maths 10 questions / 35 min; Logical 15 / 25 min; Verbal 20 / 20 min; Pseudocode 5 / 10 min; Puzzle 4 / 10 min
7 sections with sectional cutoffs, about 2 hours, offline at a centre (candidate, Jan 2025)

tips: Every section has a cutoff, so do not skip any section
Practise pseudocode tracing with loops and recursion
stages.before_next: Take one full timed mock with all sections.
stages.label: Third-party

stages.name: Online coding test for SP and DSE (also HackWithInfy)
stages.what: Three coding problems of rising difficulty in one long sitting. Your score decides SP, DSE or no offer.

format.text: 3 coding questions in 3 hours, sectional or topic-wise cutoff; easy, medium (often greedy) and hard (often DP)
3 questions in 3 hours with cutoffs per question; some drives report a 4th complex question; partial scoring exists
HackWithInfy can give pre-placement interviews for Specialist Programmer and other roles (official page, seen in search snippet)

tips: Solve the easy one fully first
Submit a working brute force for partial marks before optimising
You may use different languages for different questions
stages.before_next: Practise 10 to 15 medium DP and graph problems with a timer.
stages.label: Third-party

stages.name: Technical interview (SP/DSE)
stages.what: Live DSA problems, OOP, DBMS/SQL and project questions, usually at an Infosys campus.

format.text: 2 easy to medium DSA problems live, plus OOP, DBMS/SQL, resume and scenario questions
Resume deep dive, ML and ReactJS terms, 5th highest salary SQL, a bit-manipulation and a DFS grid problem, deadlocks and OOP (SP, 2025 batch)

tips: Know every term written on your resume
stages.before_next: Practise explaining 2 DSA solutions aloud and revise OS deadlocks.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Personal interview (Systems Engineer)
stages.what: One 20 to 25 minute interview mixing resume, project, SDLC/Agile and managerial questions.

format.text: 20 to 25 minutes, in person; final-year project, SDLC, Scrum Master, sprint planning, handling rejection, declining CGPA (Jan 2025)

tips: Be ready to explain any dip in marks honestly
Keep project explanation under 2 minutes, then go deeper if asked
stages.before_next: Revise Agile/Scrum terms and prepare your project story.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: HR interview
stages.what: Communication, cultural fit and willingness to relocate for training.

format.text: Assesses communication, fit and willingness to relocate to Mysore/Bangalore for training

tips: Carry original mark sheets, resume copy, photos and government ID
stages.before_next: Keep documents ready as listed by the eligibility page.
stages.label: Third-party

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: What is the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)?
questions.answer: The step-by-step process to build software: requirements, design, development, testing, deployment and maintenance.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: Who is a Scrum Master?
questions.answer: The person who helps a Scrum team follow the process, removes blockers and runs the ceremonies. They do not assign work like a manager.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: What is sprint planning?
questions.answer: A meeting at the start of a sprint where the team picks backlog items for the sprint and plans how to finish them.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: HR
questions.question: How do you handle rejections?
questions.answer: Accept it calmly, ask for or find the reason, learn from it and try again with a better plan. Give one real example.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: SQL
questions.question: Write a query to find the 5th highest salary in a table.
questions.answer: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM emp ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4; (checked in SQLite: salaries 600,500,400,300,300,200,100 give 200).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Given a grid of 1s (warships) and 0s (water), count the groups of warships connected up, down, left or right.
questions.answer: Number of Islands: loop over cells, start a DFS on each unvisited 1 and count how many DFS calls you start. The grid 11000/11000/00100/00011 gives 3 (checked in Python).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: OS
questions.question: What is a deadlock and how can it be prevented?
questions.answer: Processes wait on each other forever. It needs mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait; prevent it by breaking one, for example ordering resources to stop circular wait.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Pseudocode
questions.question: What is printed? s = 0; for i = 1 to 5: if i mod 2 == 0 then s = s + i*i else s = s - i; print s
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Quant
questions.question: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, how many days do they take?
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Logical
questions.question: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are bags. Conclusion: Some pens are bags. Does it follow?
options: Only if all books are bags
Cannot say from the data, but likely
questions.answer: No. The books that are bags may not include any pens.
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.answer: He doesn't like tea. With 'does' the main verb stays in base form.
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Given coin values and an amount, find the minimum number of coins to make the amount, or -1 if not possible.
questions.answer: DP: dp[0]=0, dp[x] = min(dp[x - c] + 1) over coins c. For coins [1,2,5] and amount 11 the answer is 3 (5+5+1).
questions.label: AI practice
